content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Access, entrance, or passage—most characteristically, access to God, salvation, and eternal life through Christ. A door or gate may therefore represent both the offered way of entry and the decisive boundary between those admitted and those excluded.","primary_basis":["John 10:7-9 — Jesus identifies himself as the gate/door through whom one enters and is saved.","Matthew 7:13-14; Luke 13:24 — the narrow gate represents the difficult way leading to life, contrasted with the broad way leading to destruction.","John 14:6 — although not using the door image, it commonly supports the interpretation of Christ as the exclusive way of access to the Father.","Luke 13:25-28; Matthew 25:10-12 — the shut door symbolizes the end of opportunity and exclusion from the kingdom.","Revelation 3:20 — Christ standing at the door and knocking is commonly interpreted as an invitation to fellowship, repentance, or personal reception of Christ."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"An opportunity opened by God, especially for ministry, evangelism, or effective service.","basis":["1 Corinthians 16:9","2 Corinthians 2:12","Colossians 4:3","Revelation 3:8"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Access to heaven, divine revelation, or the presence and purposes of God.","basis":["Revelation 4:1","Genesis 28:17","Psalm 24:7-10"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Judgment, exclusion, or the final closing of an opportunity to enter.","basis":["Matthew 25:10-12","Luke 13:25-28","Genesis 7:16"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Human receptivity or the inward opening of the heart to Christ.","basis":["Revelation 3:20","Acts 14:27"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Authority, civic power, security, or vulnerability, reflecting the legal and defensive role of ancient city gates.","basis":["Genesis 22:17","Ruth 4:1-11","Psalm 127:5","Isaiah 45:1-2"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The power or domain of death and hostile spiritual forces, especially in the expression “gates of Hades.”","basis":["Matthew 16:18","Isaiah 38:10"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus around the general symbolism of access, entry, and boundary, especially Christ as the entrance to salvation. There is not one fixed meaning for every occurrence: context determines whether the image emphasizes invitation, opportunity, revelation, exclusion, judgment, authority, or security."}
